core_obligations: Part (1): cite the statement that the completion is affine (proof lines 8122-8123).

Part (2): for McQuillan X, write X as the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible ring and verify the second defining property of a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space for the completion (proof lines 8124-8128).

Part (3): use the countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, produce a finitely generated ideal of the first quotient cutting out T, lift its generators, and show that any morphism from an affine scheme whose image lies in T kills a suitable product of a power of that ideal with a member of the fundamental system; conclude that the completion is the formal spectrum of the limit of those quotients and hence countably indexed (proof lines 8130-8147).

Part (4): repeat the same computation in the adic case with the fundamental system given by powers of a finitely generated ideal, and note that the author marks some details as omitted (proof lines 8149-8156).

Part (5): note that quasi-compactness of the complement is automatic in the Noetherian case, use the same description of the completion, and apply the algebra statement on completions of Noetherian rings (proof lines 8158-8165).
proof_roadmap: Part (2): the McQuillan property through the second defining condition (proof lines 8124-8128).
Part (3): the explicit description of the completion as a limit (proof lines 8130-8147).
Part (4): the adic case, same argument, details omitted (proof lines 8149-8156).
Part (5): the Noetherian case via completions of Noetherian rings (proof lines 8158-8165).
difficulty_reason: For an affine formal algebraic space X and a closed subset T of its reduction, the lemma asserts five things about the formal completion of X along T: that it is an affine formal algebraic space, that it is McQuillan when X is, that it is countably indexed when X is and the complement of T in the reduction is quasi-compact, that it is adic* under the same quasi-compactness assumption when X is, and that it is Noetherian when X is (statement lines 8093-8120). The first part is a citation, and the second follows by recognising the completion as a morphism to the spectrum of the ring satisfying the second defining property of a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 8122-8128). The substance is the third part: since X is countably indexed it is the formal spectrum of a ring with a countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, quasi-compactness of the complement of T produces a finitely generated ideal of the first quotient cutting T out, lifts of its generators are chosen, and then the universal property of the completion is used to show that the completion is the formal spectrum of the limit of the quotients of the ring by the ideals generated by the powers of the chosen ideal together with the members of the fundamental system -- an explicit computation in which the nilpotence of the images of the chosen generators is the key observation (proof lines 8130-8147). The fourth part repeats that computation verbatim in the adic case, where the fundamental system may be taken to be the powers of a single finitely generated ideal, and the author marks some details as omitted (proof lines 8149-8156). The fifth part observes that in the Noetherian case quasi-compactness of the complement is automatic, and then applies the same description together with the corresponding algebra statement on completions of Noetherian rings (proof lines 8158-8165). The claim is H2: one computation is carried out in full and its two variants are then read off in the same way, with the McQuillan and Noetherian cases reduced to cited statements.
